Welcome to this journey—one that asks us to look honestly at the world around us, and at the stories we’ve inherited about race, privilege, and silence.
You know, these conversations can feel tough. They have a way of uncovering the structures that run beneath the surface of society, and sometimes, that means facing some uncomfortable truths together.
In her powerful work, Why I'm No Longer Talking to White People About Race, Reni Eddo-Lodge invites us to dig deep into the realities of systemic racism in Britain. She doesn’t just talk about the past—she connects it to the present, reminding us that these issues aren’t relics, but living, breathing parts of everyday life.
Through personal stories and sharp historical insight, we’ll explore how identity, power, and the emotional weight of these topics shape who gets to speak up, and whose voices are too often pushed aside. What does it take to break through denial and defensiveness? And how do silence and complicity keep injustice alive?
As we move forward together, you’ll notice how class, gender, and race all blend and collide, shaping the way we experience the world—and how we talk about it. This journey isn’t just about uncovering what’s been hidden. It’s also about the courage, resilience, and agency of those who refuse to be quieted.
So, let’s open our minds and lean in with curiosity. We’re about to peel back the layers and discover what it truly means to engage honestly—and to imagine what transformative change could look like, for all of us.
